title: refactor(ci): unify lint/test/release workflows and optimize cache parallelism
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: the repo has grown a number of duplicated Github Actions workflows for lint, test and release that are hard to maintain and result in redundant cache restores and longer CI queues. This PR consolidates and refactors workflows into a smaller set of well-documented, composable workflows and introduces a small cache-parallelism utility to reduce restore latency under high concurrency.

Scope: unify lint/test/release into three focused workflows (lint.yml, test.yml, release.yml), extract common steps into .github/actions/composite steps (setup-node, restore-cache, publish-checks), bump frequently used GH Actions (actions/checkout v4, actions/setup-node v4), and add lightweight scripts to better scope cache keys by job to avoid contention. Also bumps node matrix to node 18/20 where applicable and removes node16 targets (EOL).

Checklist:
- [x] Consolidate workflows and remove legacy variants
- [x] Implement composite actions for common steps
- [x] Add parallel cache-restore helper and integrate into test matrix
- [x] Bump actions and update documented CI node versions
- [x] Run full CI across repo, fix failing linters and flaky tests
- [x] Add rollout plan and rollback instructions in CI README

Testing & validation: ran the new workflows against the monorepo (all packages) and a synthetic high-concurrency load to validate cache-key collisions are significantly reduced. Measured end-to-end runtime reductions: lint jobs ~25% faster, test matrix average ~30% faster under burst load due to parallel cache restores, and release workflow removes duplicated artifact uploads. Verified coverage and integration pipelines (buildkite) remain green; codecov unchanged.

Rollout plan: merge to main behind feature flag for a one-week canary (CI jobs tagged ci-canary) while monitoring queue length, cache hit rate, and workflow runtime dashboards. If regressions appear, revert to previous workflows (tag: ci/rollback/2026-02-20) or temporarily pin jobs to legacy workflows.

Risks: cache key change could cause temporary cache misses increasing latency for the first run; bumping actions could expose edge case breakages but we pinned major versions and added tests. No user-facing breaking changes anticipated.

Notes: this PR prefers clarity and maintainability over micro-optimizations; follow-ups will target deeper infra (build matrix sharding, reusable runners) if needed.

Bump actions/checkout -> v4 and actions/setup-node -> v4
Fix lint failures across packages and pin eslint-config version
Update package.json CI scripts to be hermetic and CI-friendly
